source: PALS first-party authored, generic-OpenMath and Lean-verified candidate set
scope_note: All cards use only real scalar arithmetic, transc1:exp, transc1:ln, relations, logic, and explicit real-membership premises. Every variable expression passed to ln has an explicit strict-positivity premise; the sole ln(exp(x+y)) card explicitly records positivity of that exponential argument.

validation_contract.generic_openmath: Every card runs statement-semantics validation, generic retrieval C14N, and exact-C14N validation while generated.
validation_contract.legacy_manifest: Generation rejects IDs and legacy C14N collisions against docs/exponent-log-number-theory-candidates.json.
validation_contract.lean: Pass --verify-lean to compile one temporary Lean file containing all 30 witnesses in pals-agent/lean-workspace.
validation_contract.local_db: Pass --verify-db --expected-db-count 401 to read-check local Draft IDs and strict/legacy C14N collisions. This command does not write the database.

excluded_backlog.item: General real-base expressions a^x and logarithms log_a(x)
excluded_backlog.reason: The current generic profile has no typed real-base exponentiation, a base-not-equal-to-one condition, or a base-order contract.
They require a complex carrier, branch data, and typed coercions; use a separate typed complex profile.

excluded_backlog.item: Unqualified logarithm product or quotient laws
excluded_backlog.reason: The high-school real logarithm laws require positive arguments. Every included variable logarithm law retains strict positivity in its proposition.

excluded_backlog.item: Numerical drill variants differing only by constants
excluded_backlog.reason: This expansion favors reusable identity, equation, inequality, and substitution patterns rather than constant substitutions.

cards.proof_strategy: Rewrite subtraction as addition of an inverse in the exponent.
sketch_steps: setup: Bind the displayed real variables and identify the exponential arguments.
rewrite: Apply the exponential addition, subtraction, or inverse identity.
normalize: Simplify the real product, quotient, or integer multiple.
domain: Use that every real exponential is strictly positive when cancellation is needed.
conclude: State the resulting real exponential equality.
cards.lean_witness: example (x y : ℝ) : Real.exp (x - y) = Real.exp x / Real.exp y := Real.exp_sub x y

example (x y z : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) (hy : 0 < y) (hz : 0 < z) : Real.log (x*y*z) = Real.log x + Real.log y + Real.log z := by
